data.cultural_impact: The name Azwan may evoke images of strong walls and fortified structures, symbolizing a protective community or a person who is well-shielded from harm. In Islamic culture, the idea of being protected is linked to the concept of being under Allah's care and guidance. This name could be given to a child as a reminder of the divine protection they receive and the need to seek refuge in Allah.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, the name Azwan can remind us of the importance of guarding our hearts and minds against negative influences and obscure desires. It can serve as a reminder of the protective nature of faith and the assurance that Allah is always by our side, shielding us from harm and guiding us towards the right path. The name Azwan can also be seen as a call to be a protector and guardian of the faith, and to help create a safe and secure environment for others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Azwan translates to "The Protector" or "The Guardian" in Arabic. This name symbolizes one who shields and safeguards, both physically and spiritually, those under their care. It also signifies a strong sense of responsibility and commitment towards protection.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The name Azwan is derived from the Arabic word for bountiful or generous, 'az-zawan', which was used to describe the fertile land along the banks of the Euphrates River in Iraq. This region was a center of Islamic civilization during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 CE).

Azwan was also the name of a major tributary that flowed into the Arabian Sea, and was an important source of water for the ancient city of Aden in Yemen. During the Aden Sultanate period (1538-1637 CE), Azwan was a prosperous port city that played a significant role in the Indian Ocean trade.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Azwan remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
